title: Join the it_companies with a string
description:
Join the it_companies with a string '#;  '.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as join_companies(companies), returning the companies joined into a single string using the separator '#; '.
examples:
>>> join_companies(['Facebook', 'Google', 'Microsoft', 'Apple', 'IBM', 'Oracle', 'Amazon'])
'Facebook#; Google#; Microsoft#; Apple#; IBM#; Oracle#; Amazon'
hints: Strings have a method for combining a list of strings using a separator.
The separator string goes in front of the .join() call, and the list goes inside the parentheses.
expected_behavior: Returns a single string with all companies joined by the separator '#; '.

hidden_tests.expected: 'Facebook#; Google#; Microsoft#; Apple#; IBM#; Oracle#; Amazon'
hidden_tests.label: seven companies joined

explanation: str.join() takes an iterable of strings and glues them together with the string it was called on placed between each pair.
